title: Scientists Confirm a Third Type of Magnetism
summary:
For almost 90 years, scientists put magnetic materials into two groups. Now they have strong proof of a third group. A team led by SLAC found the proof, and the study was published in the journal Science.

The team studied a material called manganese telluride, or MnTe. They found a twist in its magnetic structure. The twist is called chirality, and it is like the shape of a spiral staircase. That twist is a key sign of the third kind of magnetism, called altermagnetism. Lead author Daniel Jost of SLAC said the results give strong proof that this third kind is real.

Magnetism comes from a property of electrons called spin. In ferromagnets, the spins point the same way and make the field of an ordinary magnet. In antiferromagnets, found in 1933, neighboring spins point opposite ways, so their effects cancel out. In altermagnets, the spins also alternate, so they show no overall magnetism. Yet they can carry spin currents, like ferromagnets. The discovery could lead to better memory systems, quantum devices, and data centers that use less energy.
why_it_matters: This discovery could one day make the computers, phones, and game consoles you use faster and use less energy.

background_read: Magnetism comes from tiny parts inside materials called electrons, and the way their spins point decides what kind of magnet a material is.
In some magnets the spins all point the same way and make a strong magnetic field, while in others the spins point in opposite ways and cancel each other out.
Altermagnets are a third kind where the spins alternate in a twisted pattern, so they show no overall magnetism but can still carry spin currents.
